hypotheses.justification: Nothing else in the statement uses p: `red N k F : F ⊗[ℤ] intForms N k →ₗ[F] PowerSeries F` only needs `[Field F]`. The conclusion is true for every field F. The existing proof covers characteristic p prime, through `linearIndependent_redL`. That leaves characteristic 0, which can be proved as follows. `exists_basis_intForms` (it needs only `[NeZero N]`) gives a finite ℤ-basis b of intForms. Write `z i m := zc (b i) m ∈ ℤ`. The integer vectors `zcHom (b i)` are ℤ-linearly independent, because `zcHom_injective` holds and b is a basis. Suppose `∑ c i • redL (b i) = 0` in F[[X]]. Taking coefficient m gives `∑ c i * (z i m : F) = 0` for every m. Since F has characteristic 0 it is a ℚ-vector space (via `DivisionRing.toRatAlgebra`), so choose a ℚ-basis e of F. Applying `e.repr · j`, which is ℚ-linear, gives `∑ e.repr (c i) j * z i m = 0` in ℚ for every m. This mirrors the existing proof, with ZMod p replaced by ℚ. Multiply by a common denominator D to get integers `d i` with `∑ d i * z i m = 0` for all m. Then `zcHom (∑ d i • b i) = 0`, so `∑ d i • b i = 0`, so every `d i = 0`, hence every `e.repr (c i) j = 0`, hence every `c i = 0`. So the redL (b i) are F-linearly independent in every characteristic. The final step of the current proof (expand y in the basis `Algebra.TensorProduct.basis F b` and use independence) then works unchanged. Removing `[CharP F p]` makes p and `[Fact p.Prime]` unused, but they remain valid arguments.

Delete only this binder and keep `[CharP F p]`. Since F is a field, `CharP.char_is_prime_or_zero` gives that p is prime or p = 0. If p is prime, the existing proof applies; the `Fact` instance can be rebuilt from the primality just obtained. If p = 0, F has characteristic 0, and the argument above applies: pick a ℚ-basis of F, reduce the F-linear relation to ℚ-linear relations among the integer q-expansion vectors `zc (b i)`, clear denominators, and use `zcHom_injective` together with the fact that b is a ℤ-basis. So the statement stays true and provable. Each of `[Fact p.Prime]` and `[CharP F p]` can be deleted on its own, and both can also be deleted together.
